annotation_description: With Mishra's Bauble, looking at your own library top card is generally better when you have Brainstorm in hand and a fetchland (Misty Rainforest) on the battlefield. Knowing your own top card lets you make better decisions about when to Brainstorm and how to sequence fetch + Brainstorm for optimal card selection. Looking at the opponent's top card provides marginal information that rarely changes your decisions on turn 1. Additionally, with Dragon's Rage Channeler in hand (which has surveil), knowing your own top card would help plan surveil decisions.

Playing Wasteland instead of Plateau means the player cannot cast any of their 2-drop spells this turn (Sand Scout needs 1W, Amped Raptor needs 1R, Goblin Bombardment needs 1R - all require colored mana from both lands). With Plateau + Wasteland, they only have one colored source and one colorless source, so they can't cast any 2-mana spell. With two Plateaus, they could cast any of their three 2-drops immediately. The reasoning even starts to identify this problem but cuts off. Falling behind on tempo by a full turn in Legacy is meaningful.

Casting Amped Raptor into an opponent with an untapped Misty Rainforest (likely representing Daze or other interaction) is risky. More importantly, casting a creature before combat is generally suboptimal when holding tricks like Swords to Plowshares - though here there's nothing to attack with. The bigger question is whether Sand Scout would have been better: the opponent has an uncracked Misty Rainforest, so they likely have 1 land vs Sonnet Spike's 2, meaning Sand Scout's ETB would trigger to search for a Desert, providing ramp and setting up the token-generation ability. Amped Raptor's cascade-like ability is high variance and the energy may not find anything castable, while Sand Scout provides guaranteed value with the land advantage.

Casting Sand Scout before combat means the opponent sees the additional creature before blocks/combat decisions. With Ocelot Pride (lifelink) and Amped Raptor ready to attack, it would be better to attack first, then cast Sand Scout in second main phase. Attacking with Ocelot Pride could gain life (triggering its end-step token creation) and the opponent only has Misty Rainforest with no blockers visible. Additionally, casting creatures before combat when holding Swords to Plowshares (a combat trick of sorts) is generally suboptimal sequencing - you want to leave mana open and present fewer cards to the opponent's potential responses. However, Sand Scout's ETB ability to search for a Desert (opponent has 1 land, you have 3, so it won't trigger) makes pre-combat casting slightly less impactful. The main concern is giving information and not attacking first.

Sonnet Spike declined to attack with Amped Raptor (2/1 first strike) and Ocelot Pride (1/1 first strike, lifelink) when the opponent had only a Misty Rainforest and no creatures on board. The opponent has no blockers, so attacking is completely free. Ocelot Pride attacking would deal 1 damage and gain 1 life, which triggers its end step ability to create a 1/1 Cat token. The Amped Raptor would deal 2 damage. That's 3 free damage plus a token. The reasoning about summoning sickness is wrong - these creatures were clearly available to attack (the game offered them as attackers), meaning they've been on the battlefield since at least the previous turn. The opponent does have Daze/Brainstorm potential from their blue mana, but that doesn't affect combat.

Haiku Valley appears to have missed their entire turn 3 - they have a land in hand (Scalding Tarn or Volcanic Island) they could have played, and they could have deployed Dragon's Rage Channeler (a key 1-drop) or Stormchaser's Talent. Instead they're discarding to hand size again at end of turn, meaning they took no actions on their turn. The opponent has developed a strong board with Ocelot Pride, Amped Raptor, and Sand Scout while Haiku Valley has only Misty Rainforest. As for the discard choice itself, discarding Stormchaser's Talent is reasonable since they have two copies, but the real blunder is having done nothing this turn.

After casting Voice of Victory, Sonnet Spike skipped the attack phase with Amped Raptor (2/1), Ocelot Pride (1/1 lifelink), Sand Scout (2/2), and the newly cast Voice of Victory (1/3 with Mobilize 2) against an opponent with zero creatures. This missed at least 5 damage (possibly more with Mobilize tokens), plus missed triggering Ocelot Pride's end-step token generation via lifelink damage.
Opponent has Wasteland on board. Playing Volcanic Island directly exposes it to being destroyed. Fetchlands are safer against Wasteland since they can be cracked in response.

Dragon's Rage Channeler is a 1/1 that needs noncreature spells to surveil and reach delirium. The opponent has Voice of Victory on the battlefield, which reads 'Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn.' While this is the opponent's postcombat main (Haiku Valley's turn), that restriction only applies during the opponent's turn, so casting here is legal. However, the real issue is sequencing and board state assessment. The opponent has a threatening board with Ocelot Pride, Amped Raptor, Sand Scout, Voice of Victory, and Wasteland. DRC as a 1/1 does very little here defensively. More importantly, Stormchaser's Talent would create a 1/1 prowess token AND set up future value with level-ups and graveyard recursion. Playing Stormchaser's Talent first is better because it creates a body AND the prowess token benefits from subsequent spell casts. Additionally, the player should have played Scalding Tarn from hand first (land drop) before casting any spell, to have more mana available and to be able to crack the fetch for delirium fuel or mana fixing later.

message: Select a Mountain or Plains card
annotation_description: Fetched a third Plateau instead of a basic land. With two Plateaus already providing both colors, a basic Plains would provide the same mana while being immune to Wasteland. The hand is W-heavy (Swords to Plowshares, two Sand Scouts) making Plains the better basic, and having three nonbasic lands makes the mana base unnecessarily vulnerable.

With Voice of Victory on the opponent's board ('Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn'), Haiku Valley needs to use their mana efficiently on their own turn. The opponent has Ocelot Pride (1/1 with lifelink) which will create tokens at end step if it gains life - meaning if it attacks and connects, it snowballs. Lightning Bolt on Ocelot Pride is the highest-impact play here, preventing the token generation engine from getting out of control. Brainstorm is a strong card but doesn't address the board pressure - the opponent already has Sand Scout, Voice of Victory, Amped Raptor, Ocelot Pride, and a Sand Warrior token. Additionally, Brainstorm could have been cast on the opponent's turn (Voice of Victory only prevents casting during opponent's turn, not your own turn... wait, actually Voice says 'Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn' - so Haiku Valley can't cast on Sonnet Spike's turn). Still, Lightning Bolt removing Ocelot Pride before it can attack and generate tokens is more urgent than card selection. The DRC surveil trigger happens either way.

Cracking Misty Rainforest before Brainstorm resolves wastes the key Brainstorm+fetchland synergy. The fetch shuffle should happen AFTER Brainstorm resolves to shuffle away the two worst cards put back on top.

Playing Scalding Tarn instead of Volcanic Island when holding Ponder in hand. Volcanic Island provides the same mana immediately without costing life, and saving the fetchland allows shuffling after a future Ponder for better card selection. Additionally, Volcanic Island untapped gives access to both U and R mana right away.

Skipped the attack phase entirely with a dominant board (Amped Raptor, Ocelot Pride, Sand Scout, Voice of Victory with Mobilize 2, Sand Warrior token) against only a single Dragon's Rage Channeler. Voice of Victory prevents the opponent from casting spells during Sonnet Spike's turn, meaning no combat tricks, no Daze, no Lightning Bolt. Attacking would deal massive damage (potentially 7+ with Mobilize warriors) and Ocelot Pride's lifelink would trigger end-step token creation.

Amped Raptor is just a 2/1 body that has already used its ETB ability. Ocelot Pride is an engine piece with lifelink that creates tokens at end step whenever life is gained, and with Voice of Victory's Mobilize creating tokens, this can snowball. Killing the engine piece is far more impactful than removing a vanilla 2/1 first striker.

Declined to Swords to Plowshares a 3/3 Dragon's Rage Channeler that's attacking unblocked, taking 3 damage unnecessarily. With a dominant board (Ocelot Pride, Voice of Victory, Sand Scout, Sand Warrior token) and the opponent having very limited resources, removing their only creature now would effectively lock the game. DRC with surveil also helps the opponent dig for answers.

Playing Volcanic Island directly into opponent's untapped Wasteland is risky. Misty Rainforest would be safer as it can be cracked in response to Wasteland, still providing access to blue/red mana while protecting the dual land for later.

With Ponder's ordering, Force of Will was chosen first meaning it goes to the bottom of the three cards, so it won't be drawn. Given the opponent's threatening board (Ocelot Pride, Voice of Victory, Sand Scout with token) and Voice of Victory preventing spells during opponent's turn, Force of Will is the most impactful card to draw immediately - it's the premier answer/protection spell and having it in hand is critical for surviving.

With 4 mana available (3 Plateaus + Wasteland), Sonnet Spike only cast Goblin Bombardment (1R), leaving 2 mana unused when they had multiple excellent 2-drops in hand. Hexing Squelcher would provide uncounterability for future spells and ward for all creatures against a blue deck, and could have been cast alongside Goblin Bombardment.

Declined to chump block Dragon's Rage Channeler (3/3 with delirium) with a 1/1 token. Taking 3 damage (17→14) when the opponent likely has access to burn spells makes life total relevant. A 1/1 token is generally worth less than 3 life points.

Ocelot Pride is the key engine generating exponential token advantage each end step when life is gained (it has lifelink). Killing Sand Scout removes a 2/2 body and its land-graveyard trigger, but Ocelot Pride will snowball the board with tokens every turn it attacks and connects. With Voice of Victory creating attacking warriors, the board is already spiraling.

Haiku Valley cast Brainstorm in response to their own Lightning Bolt on the stack, spending mana and a card reactively when there was no pressing need. While Brainstorm is a good card, casting it here before resolving the Lightning Bolt doesn't accomplish much strategically - the Lightning Bolt was already on the stack targeting Sonnet Spike's board/life. More importantly, Brainstorm without a subsequent shuffle (fetchland crack) is less valuable, and they could have saved it for a more critical moment or cast it at end of turn with fetch shuffle available. The Brainstorm could have been saved to be cast alongside a fetchland crack for maximum value, rather than using it mid-stack where it doesn't change the combat math or protect anything.

Put Murktide Regent back with Brainstorm despite it being castable next turn for just UU with 7+ cards in graveyard for delve. With fetchlands available to shuffle, the put-back cards get shuffled away anyway, making it better to keep Murktide in hand where it's guaranteed accessible.
